Concrete gravity.requires: mass resisting by weight on a sound foundation
Concrete gravity.provides: tolerance of overtopping, no erodible body, dependence on foundation shear

Earthfill embankment.requires: compacted fill with a low-permeability core
Earthfill embankment.provides: no tolerance of overtopping, susceptibility to internal erosion, wide footprint

Tailings storage facility.provides: saturated fine waste, liquefiable, never decommissioned during operation

Concrete arch.requires: a narrow gorge with competent abutments
Concrete arch.provides: thin efficient structure, total dependence on abutment rock, tolerance of overtopping

Overtopping in flood.provides: erosion of any erodible crest, hours of warning from catchment

Internal erosion.provides: progressive concealed development, days to weeks, detectable by instruments

Foundation sliding.provides: sudden movement of an intact structure, no erosion

Liquefaction under seismic load.requires: saturated loose material and ground shaking
Liquefaction under seismic load.provides: instantaneous loss of strength, no warning, total release

Piezometer pressure rise.provides: early warning of seepage and pore pressure, no visual confirmation

Seepage turbidity increase.provides: direct evidence of material being carried, specific to erosion

No indicator observed.requires: either no instrumentation or a mechanism giving none

Populated town.provides: life safety as the governing concern, evacuation feasible with warning

Farmland only.provides: economic loss, no immediate life safety concern

Another dam in cascade.provides: risk of progressive failure, engineering response possible

Uninhabited valley.provides: no consequence beyond the asset itself

Controlled drawdown.requires: outlet capacity and days of time
Controlled drawdown.provides: reduction of load, loss of stored water

Emergency spillway operation.requires: an existing spillway and rising water
Emergency spillway operation.provides: immediate relief of overtopping risk only

Downstream evacuation.requires: population at risk and warning time
Downstream evacuation.provides: life safety, no effect on the structure

Buttressing works.requires: weeks of construction and stable conditions
Buttressing works.provides: structural strengthening, useless in an emergency

_v1_notes.DAM TYPE|FAILURE MECHANISM: concrete gravity and arch dams are N for overtopping (both tolerate it) and N for internal erosion (no erodible body) and N for liquefaction (no saturated loose material). Only foundation sliding applies to both. An earthfill embankment is N for liquefaction unless saturated and loose, which is the tailings case; here N. A tailings facility is vulnerable to all four.
_v1_notes.DAM TYPE|WARNING INDICATOR: concrete gravity and arch are N for piezometer pressure rise as a governing indicator - pore pressure in an embankment body is the relevant measurement, not in mass concrete.
_v1_notes.DAM TYPE|INTERVENTION: a tailings facility is N for controlled drawdown (the stored material is solid waste, not water) and N for spillway operation.
_v1_notes.FAILURE MECHANISM|WARNING INDICATOR: overtopping is N for piezometers and N for turbidity - it is a water level event, warned by catchment forecast; here crest settlement and no-indicator are the listed possibilities. Internal erosion is N for no-indicator, being precisely the mechanism instruments detect. Foundation sliding is N for piezometers and turbidity. Liquefaction gives no indicator at all, so the first three are N.
_v1_notes.FAILURE MECHANISM|INTERVENTION: overtopping is N for buttressing (too slow). Internal erosion and foundation sliding are both N for spillway operation, which addresses water level only. Liquefaction is N for drawdown, spillway and buttressing alike - it is instantaneous, leaving only evacuation.
_v1_notes.WARNING INDICATOR|INTERVENTION: no-indicator-observed is N for every intervention, since none can be triggered by an absent warning.
_v1_notes.DOWNSTREAM EXPOSURE|INTERVENTION: farmland, cascade and uninhabited valley are all N for downstream evacuation - there is no population to evacuate.
